PAGE	137
P	<i>Most people hope for a quiet life. They spend their days a-worrying: about a leaky roof,</i> <i>a sick child, their crops. But you aren't like most people—you're on a different path. A path</i> <i>to adventure! There's greatness in you. Let's hope you live long enough for everyone else to see it.</i>
HR
H2	Background (Choose 1)
C	<b>IMPETUOUS YOUTH</b> Stonetop has always been home, but you chafe at the demands of mundane life and have always longed for more. Excitement! Danger!
P	When you <b><i>make a move and come up short</i></b>, you can give it your all and turn a 6- into a 7-9, a 7-9 into a 10+, and (if it matters), a 10-11 into a 12+. But if you do, pick 1 (the GM will fill in the details):
B	You get hurt (2d4 damage and an actual injury)
B	You cause collateral damage, endanger others, or otherwise escalate the situation
B	Something on your person is lost or breaks
C	<b>DRIVEN</b> You once led a simple life, but something happened. Something changed you, burdened you with terrible purpose. What was it? Choose 1:
C	A loved one was killed or abducted
C	Someone gave their life to save you
C	Your idol sacrificed themselves to save many
C	You stumbled upon a dark mystery
C	You must make amends for a terrible mistake You always have the option of Burning Brightly; you can spend 2 XP after you roll to add +1, even if you don't have enough XP to level.
C	<b>DESTINED</b> ◇◇◇ Fate has laid her hand upon you. Choose 3-4 of the items below to describe your destiny:
C	anointed marked at birth your coming foretold
C	destroy discover free protect restore
C	unify blood civilization darkness
C	earth & stone fire ice light life storms
C	war water the Fae the gods the Makers
C	the Stone the Things Below At the <b><i>start of a session</i></b>, roll +Omens: <b>on a 7+</b>, lose all Omens and the GM will describe a vision or portent that points toward your fate and/or clarifies your current situation; also, <b>on a 10+</b>, ask the GM a follow-up question and get a clear, helpful answer;
P	<b><i>on a 6-</i></b>, don't mark XP, hold +1 Omen, and tell us of your recent nightmares or a troubling vision, and how your fears play into them.
P	<b><i>Until your destiny is fulfilled</i></b>, treat a 6- on Death's Door as a 7-9, and a 7-9 as a 10+.
H2	Instinct (Choose 1)
C	<b>DEFIANCE</b> To refuse to back down, give up, give in.
HR
C	<b>DOUBT</b> To question yourself, your actions, your worth.
HR
C	<b>EARNESTNESS</b> To prove yourself, to yourself and others.
HR
C	<b>OPTIMISM</b> To assume the best, and that things are simple.
HR
C	<b>SACRIFICE</b> To put the needs/wants of others above your own.
HR
H2	Appearance
P	Choose 1 on each line, or make something up:
C	still a child young & beautiful all grown up
C	confident voice earnest voice quiet voice
C	big scrawny sinewy slender thick
C	back unbowed jaw firmly set soulful eyes
H2	Place of origin and name
P	Stonetop is your home, or close enough, but where are you (or your family) from originally? Pick 1 and a name to match (or make up something similar).
C	<b>Stonetop</b>: Anwen, Caradoc, Dafyd, Glenys, Madoc, Morwenna, Siwan, or Wynfor
C	<b>Barrier Pass</b>: Bala, Cotota, Ganzorig, Gerelma, Ibahka, Jungshoi, Mukhali, or Taichu
C	<b>Steplands</b> (Hillfolk): Annic, Cosette, Denl, Hugenne, Jag, Marc, Oanz, or Sandre
C	<b>Gordin's Delve</b>: Pick a name from any list
C	<b>Marshedge</b>: Bridin, Clian, Engis, Fearghul, Lan, Neasa, Nill, or Una
C	<b>Lygos or some other point south</b>: Chara, Davud, Korina, Omid, Parvaneh, Tamir, Takish, or Yannis

H2	Special possessions (Pick 2)
HR
C	<b>A heap of expectations</b>: of little use
C	<b>A good dog</b>, follower ( <i>retriever</i> or <i>herder</i>, <i>keen-nosed</i>, <i>clever</i>); HP 6; Damage d6 (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>); <b>Instinct</b> to play; Cost: affection.
C	<b>Husbandry tools</b>: brushes, muzzles, collars, feed, ◇ whips, ◇ bridles, etc. Gain advantage to Persuade domestic beasts (livestock, dogs, etc.).
C	<b>Smithy</b> (or access to it): iron goods, ingots, thick gloves, ◇ tongs, ◇ bellows, an anvil, etc.
C	<b>Stoneworker's tools</b>: chisels, drills, ◇ prybars, ◇ spikes, ◇ block & tackles, wheelbarrow, etc.
C	<b>Personal token, fraught with meaning</b>: (pick 1) ◇◇ A shield, bearing ___'s crest
C	◇ A wool cloak, woven just for you by ___
C	A letter, spattered with tears & blood
C	A flute, a gift from someone you loved
C	A fine locket, holding a strand of hair
C	A tinderbox, lovingly engraved
C	<b>Tannery</b> (or access to it): lime, acid, salts, thick gloves, ◇ a boiled leather cuirass (1 armor), etc.

H2	Moves
HR
P	You start with Anger is a Gift, Potential for Greatness, and 2 other moves of your choice.
HR
CX	<b>ANGER IS A GIFT</b> ◇◇
P	When you <b><i>burn with righteous anger</i></b> (see Fear & Anger on back of playbook), hold 2 Resolve. You can spend your Resolve 1-for-1 to:
B	Set aside fear and doubt to do what must be done
B	Act suddenly, catching them off-guard
B	Inspire allies or bystanders to follow your lead
B	Strike hard (+1d4 damage, <i>forceful</i>)
B	Keep your footing, position, and/or your course despite what befalls you
C2	<b>SPEAK TRUTH TO POWER</b>
P	(Requires Anger is a Gift)
P	When you <b><i>demand that someone does what is</i></b> <b><i>clearly good and right</i></b>, you have advantage to Persuade. If they refuse, gain +1 Resolve.
C	<b>BETTER PART OF VALOR</b> When you <b><i>are outnumbered or facing a foe bigger</i></b> <b><i>than you</i></b>, you have advantage to hide from, escape from, or sneak past them.
C	<b>I GET KNOCKED DOWN</b> When you <b><i>take damage despite your best efforts to</i></b> <b><i>avoid it</i></b>, you can choose to halve the damage but pick 1 of the following:
B	You lose something (footing, grip, etc.)
B	Something on your person breaks
B	You're out of it for a moment Whatever you choose, the GM will describe the details.
C2	<b>BUT I GET UP AGAIN</b>
P	(Requires I Get Knocked Down)
P	When you <b><i>use I Get Knocked Down</i></b>, you have advantage on your next roll against whatever dealt the damage and your next blow against them does +1d4 damage.
C	<b>IMPROVED STAT</b> Each time you take this move, increase one of your stats by 1 (to a max of +2).
C	<b>IN OVER YOUR HEAD</b> When <b><i>another PC rescues you from danger</i></b>, mark XP.
C	<b>IRON WILL</b> When you <b><i>are subject to mind control or magic</i></b> <b><i>that affects your feelings</i></b>, you can take 1d4 damage (ignoring armor) to disregard its influence.
C	<b>INQUIRING MINDS</b> When you <b><i>seek out and receive honest advice</i></b>, gain advantage on your next roll to follow that advice.
C	<b>NEVER GONNA KEEP ME DOWN</b> ◇ When you <b><i>have 5 or fewer current HP</i></b>, you impose disadvantage on any damage you take.
P	Once per session, when you are at Death's Door, don't roll. You get a 10+.
CX	<b>POTENTIAL FOR GREATNESS</b>
P	(Requires the Would-be Hero)
P	Once per level, <b><i>when you roll a stat and get a 10+</i></b>, mark one of the following (note the level during which you marked it). You don't have to mark them in order.
C	Increase the stat you rolled by 1, to a max of +2 (at level ___)
C	Increase the stat you rolled by 1, to a max of +2 (at level ___)
C	Increase the stat you rolled by 1, to a max of +2 (at level ___)
C	Increase the stat you rolled by 1, to a max of +2 (at level ___)
C	Increase your max HP by 4 (at level ___)
C	Increase your damage die to a d8 (at level ___)
PAGE	139
C	<b>RESOURCEFUL</b> When you <b><i>Defy Danger and roll a 6-</i></b>, ask the GM a question from Seek Insight after they describe what happens. Gain advantage on your next roll to act on the answer.
C	<b>SOMETHING TO REMEMBER ME BY</b> When you <b><i>spend Readiness (from Defend) to strike</i></b> <b><i>back at an attacker</i></b>, you deal +1d4 damage and scar, mark, or diminish them in some way (the GM will say how, or ask you to).
C	<b>TOUGH LOVE</b> When you <b><i>honestly think another PC is in the wrong</i></b> <b><i>and call them on it</i></b>, they have disadvantage on any rolls against you until you two work it out.
C	<b>UNDERESTIMATED</b> As long as you <b><i>avoid overt hostility</i></b>, no enemy will consider you a threat.
P	When you <b><i>first make your move against an enemy</i></b> <b><i>who underestimates you</i></b>, you have advantage.
C	<b>UP WITH PEOPLE</b> ◇◇ | ◇ When you <b><i>converse with someone</i></b> (PC or NPC) you can hold 2 Rapport with them. If you do, they hold 1 Rapport with you. During the conversation, either of you can spend 1 Rapport to ask the other player one of the following and get an honest answer.
Q	What weighs you down or holds you back?
Q	What drives you forward?
Q	What lesson would you have me learn?
Q	What do you think of me, truly?
C2	<b>VERSATILE</b>
P	(Requires level 2+, the Would-be Hero)
P	Choose a move from any other playbook, as long as you meet its requirements. You can pick from a different playbook each time. You can't take Improved
P	Stat or Superior Stat.
P	* The first time you use any move marked with an asterisk (*), cross off "Would-be" on the front page.
C	<b>A FORCE TO BE RECKONED WITH*</b> (Requires level 6+; replaces Underestimated) Any intelligent creature who looks you in the eye or hears the steel in your voice instinctively knows that you are a force to be reckoned with, and treats you appropriately.
P	When you <b><i>Defy Danger against something trying to</i></b> <b><i>harm or constrain you</i></b>, on a 12+ you turn the tables on them (the GM will say how, or ask you to).
C	<b>BIG DAMN HERO*</b> (Requires level 6+; replaces In Over Your Head) When you <b><i>first leap into danger to protect someone</i></b>, don't roll to Defend. Instead, treat it as though you rolled a 10+.
P	When you <b><i>Defend</i></b>, you can spend 1 Readiness to lock eyes with an attacker; they have disadvantage on damage rolls against you and your ward for the rest of the fight.
C	<b>SUPERIOR STAT</b> (Requires all 6 marks in Potential for Greatness) Increase one of your stats by +1 (to a max of +3).
C	<b>UNDAUNTED*</b> (Requires level 6+; replaces Better Part of Valor) When you <b><i>are outnumbered or facing a foe bigger</i></b> <b><i>than you</i></b>, you get +1 armor and deal +1d6 damage.
C	<b>VOICE OF EXPERIENCE*</b> (Requires level 6+; replaces Inquiring Minds) When <b><i>another PC comes to you for advice and you</i></b> <b><i>tell them what you think is best</i></b>, they have advantage on their first roll to follow your advice.
P	When you <b><i>Seek Insight</i></b>, you can always ask, "What is about to happen?" for free, even on a 6-.

H2	Fear & anger
P	What do you fear most? (choose 1, maybe 2)
C	Fire, burning, the smell of charred flesh
C	That they won't take you seriously
C	That you really aren't cut out for this
C	The death of your family or loved ones
C	Being alone and helpless
C	Violence, bloodshed, and pain
C	Monsters
C	What you're capable of
C	What you must do What makes you burn with righteous anger?
P	(choose 2, maybe 3)
C	Bullying, slavery, and oppression
C	Wanton cruelty and unnecessary suffering
C	Injustice and inequality
C	Cowardice, treachery, and selfishness
C	The despoiling of beauty and innocence
C	Threats to your loved ones
C	Violence to children, animals, the innocent
C	Perversions of nature
P	When did your fear or anger last cause you trouble?
P	What did you do?
P	How did it turn out?
H2	Introductions
P	Wait here for everyone else. When everyone's ready, take turns introducing your characters. When <b><i>someone reveals something and you want to know</i></b> <b><i>more</i></b>, ask them about it. When <b><i>someone asks you a</i></b> <b><i>question</i></b>, answer it truthfully.
STEP	1	On your first turn, <b>introduce yourself</b> by name, pronouns, background, origin, and appearance.
STEP	2	On your second turn, <b>describe your special</b> <b>possessions</b> and how you contribute to the village (beyond working the fields).
STEP	3	On your third turn, <b>tell us of your fear & anger</b>, and of the last time they caused you trouble.
STEP	4	On your next turn, <b>answer one of the following</b>, naming one or more NPCs who live in Stonetop.
C	Whose heart do you hope to win?
C	Who is counting on you?
C	Who quietly understands the path you are on?
C	Who do you intend to prove wrong?
STEP	5	Go around again. Answer another question from 4, or pass. When everyone has passed, go on.
STEP	6	On your next turn, <b>ask your fellow PCs one of</b> <b>these</b>. When others ask you, answer as you like.
C	Which one of you is my closest, truest friend?
C	Which one of you believes in me, despite it all?
C	Which one of you has promised to teach me?
C	Which one of you have I hurt, through what I have done or what I've failed to do?
STEP	7	Go around again. Ask another question from 6, or pass. When everyone has passed, go on.
STEP	8	Add your home to the steading playbook. When everyone is done, let spring break forth!
